title: Capacity-swap sprint tap and price-hedge v2
content:
Purpose:
Quick working worksheet to test a short-duration capacity-swap (internal FTEs reallocated to surge lanes) combined with a small freelance pool and a dynamic price-hedge (temporary customer price floor / credit cushion) to blunt a token-price/latency shock scenario for Q2–Q3 2026.

Top-level hypothesis:
If we allow a 6-week sprint-tap of 8 FTEs from low-priority feature teams + a 50-person-hour/week freelance pool, and simultaneously apply a 10% temporary surcharge floor for top 5% of burst customers with credit offsets, we can buy ~4 weeks of steady-state runway for core Dedicated latency SLAs at an incremental gross burn that is < 0.6% of monthly Opex.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Average fully-loaded FTE cost (comp + burden + infra allocation): $30,000/month
- Freelance pool blended rate: $100/hour (includes agency fees)
- Typical token-driven incremental cost during surge: 0.004 $/token (gpu compute + infra)
- Token surge profile (worst 72h): +250M tokens/day networked across top 50 customers
- Price-hedge instrument: temporary surcharge floor of +10% on billable token rate for top 5% accounts with automatic credit coupon equal to 6% of surcharge applied to future invoice if surge persists beyond 6 weeks

Phased plan (6-week sprint tap):
Week 0 (prep): communication to Eng leads, identify 8 FTEs (2 infra, 2 serving-runtime, 2 SRE, 2 product ops) who can be reassigned with minimal feature impact.
Weeks 1–4: temporary reassignment to surge-handling (rebalancing capacity, kernel tuning, rapid KV-cache rollout). Freelance pool engaged to cover monitoring/playbook ops (avg 50 hours/week).
Weeks 5–6: taper; reassign back to original teams, capture run-rate delta metrics.

Crunch numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Incremental FTE cost for 8 FTEs over 4 weeks: (30,000 / 4) * 8 = $60,000
- Freelance cost (4 weeks): 50 hrs/week * $100 * 4 = $20,000
- Total direct labor incremental: $80,000
- Expected avoided burst compute spend (if surge mitigated): assume 250M tokens/day * 7 days surge peak * 0.004 $/token = $7,000,000 (this is unrealistic upper bound; more realistic capture at 2% avoided = $140,000)
- Net expected delta (conservative): avoided $140,000 - incremental $80,000 = +$60,000 benefit to gross margin for surge period

Price-hedge cashflow model (simplified):
- If surcharge floor applied to top 5% of customers yields immediate uplift of incremental 10% on billings for that cohort; assume cohort monthly bill = $4M -> surcharge yield = $400k/month
- Apply credit coupon (6% of surcharge) as deferred credit if surge lasts >6 weeks; expected deferred liability = $24k/month (if fully applied)
- Net short term receipts available to cover surge mitigation ops: ~$376k/month (conservative take rate 60% -> $225k)

Trigger rules (operational):
- Trigger A: 7-day rolling token volume for top-50 customers > +40% vs baseline for 3 consecutive days -> start sprint-tap and freelance pool activation.
- Trigger B: sustained +25% 14-day token uplift OR compute spot price > 1.6x baseline for 48 hours -> enable surcharge floor for identified cohort and notify finance + sales.
- Escalation: if mitigation does not reduce 7-day uplift to <20% after 10 days, engage regional Dedicated burst pool and evaluate further pricing actions.

Metrics to capture (during and after):
- Daily tokens avoided attributed to KV-cache changes and routing policies (manual attribution is OK for this working doc)
- Latency P99 for canary routes (pre, during, post)
- Incremental infra spend (spot invoices) and freelance payouts
- Net MRR delta from surcharge and coupon redemptions (realized vs deferred)
- Feature velocity delta for donor teams (sprint stories impacted)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: donor teams fall behind on critical milestones -> Mitigate: limit donors to non-blocking backlog slices and define success criteria for return.
- Risk: surcharge causes churn in price-sensitive customers -> Mitigate: apply only to co-horted burst cohort (top 5%) with explicit communications and sunset clause.
- Risk: attribution noise (hard to measure avoided tokens) -> Mitigate: conservative capture (use 2% avoided baseline) and require engineering annotation of mitigations.

Decision points for Finance/Leadership (timeline):
- Approve up to $120k one-time mitigation budget (covers FTE adjustments + freelance + contingency) — decision within 48 hours of trigger.
- Approve temporary surcharge floor language and marketing copy for top cohort (legal review required) — decision within 72 hours.
- Post-mortem 8 weeks after taper: compute realized ROI and recommend whether to build this into an annual surge playbook.

Open questions (for Product & Sales):
1) Which exact billing SKUs will surcharge apply to? (token-by-token vs bundled route?)
2) What is the customer-facing explanation and what coupon behavior preserves trust?
3) Can we automate donor-FTE selection in the org chart to avoid ad-hoc asks?

Appendix (quick sensitivity slices):
- If freelance cost rises to $150/hr -> incremental freelance = $30k -> net benefit flips negative in conservative capture case.
- If avoided tokens capture is actually 1% of peak -> avoided $70k -> still slightly negative vs labor but preserves latency SLA (qualitative benefit).
- If surcharge take rate is 30% not 60% -> available short-term receipts fall to ~112k/month -> still useful as buffer but not self-funding.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Finance (Ava Chen): finalize budget overlay and approval cadence.
- Eng leads (Marcus Lee): nominate donor FTEs and define minimal handover docs.
- SRE (Priya Nambiar): author playbook for rapid KV-cache rollout and surge routing.
- Sales/RevOps (Diego Alvarez): draft customer communication for surcharge floor and coupon.

Notes to self: keep this lightweight and iteratively instrument one small cohort before broadening. Capture granular timestamps for any surge remedial changes for better attribution.

Revision history: v1 initial sketch 2025-11-02 by Ava Chen; v2 conservative numbers and trigger rules added 2026-03-15 by Ava Chen.
